principle: A task is eligible for agent scoring only when its scoring machinery demonstrates both sensitivity to a valid reviewed solution and rejection of a no-op or known-broken baseline, while the prompt fully specifies the graded behavior.

common_gates.requirement: Every normative brief requirement maps to one or more explicit acceptance assertions, and every scored assertion maps back to a brief requirement. Undocumented test-only requirements are forbidden.

A reviewed reference/witness patch applied to the exact pristine base passes every required target oracle; an empty/no-op or seeded-defect baseline fails the intended target oracle. A failure caused by unrelated infrastructure does not satisfy either side.

At least one qualified engineer who did not author the tests can solve from the task brief and permitted references without access to hidden test logic, gold patches or verifier internals; two reviewers independently assess ambiguity and requirement sufficiency.

Candidate changes cannot modify the evaluator, tests, hidden fixtures, scoring policy, expected outputs, dependency cache or runner configuration. Only the candidate patch is transferred into the evaluation image.

Reapply the exact candidate patch to a fresh evaluator-owned image derived from the frozen base; rerun all required tests and journeys after candidate execution. Preserve both in-run and pristine regrade outcomes.

Deny access to fixing commits, hidden source, verifier policy and unapproved code-host endpoints. Permit only the model endpoint and explicitly declared fixture-local services when the task design requires them.
Label public, controller-only and hidden exposure before evaluation. Public pilot tasks cannot later be represented as hidden holdout results; hold out whole task families and interaction patterns.
For repair/maintenance tasks, verify the target defect changes as expected, a placebo does not receive credit, and unrelated contract invariants remain preserved.

rules: A task is runnable only after its two-sided validity gate and all execution/evidence gates pass.
A two-sided validity pass does not imply browser, accessibility, security or task-score qualification.
Infrastructure failures and inconclusive outcomes are never silently converted into pass or product failure.
Publish per-task evidence and failure reasons; do not hide excluded tasks or denominator changes.

limitations: This is a task-quality protocol, not an execution result or benchmark score.
Reference patches are witnesses of satisfiability, not necessarily the only acceptable implementation.
The witness patch and hidden scoring policy must remain outside the agent workspace during evaluation.
The protocol must be integrated with trusted isolated execution and independent oracle replay before it can promote SFEB tasks.
